name: Thread & Co.
blurb: A mid-priced apparel brand with 900 stores and a web shop. Everything is made at 40 supplier factories in Karvan and two other countries, and the biggest Karvan factory employs 2,000 people. Founder Elodie Marchetti started with one denim line and holds 26% of the vote.

exposure.text: Disbarred if the board is caught hiding facts while he sits on it.

secrets.text: Never be on a board that's caught hiding facts.
Your firm does Thread & Co.'s trademark work by the hour. One caught fact brings in outside counsel, so none may be caught.

exposure.text: Loses the next vote if the board delays factory payment or moves orders away from union factories.

secrets.text: A supplier wage floor passes before the game ends.
You were granted stock options last year. The stock must end above where it started.

exposure.text: Investors pull money from his fund if the stock ends below where it started.

secrets.text: Pass a buyback of $30M or more in any round.
Your fund quietly owns a rival fast-fashion brand. Thread & Co.'s stock must finish in the bottom half.

directors.name: Camille Roux
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.home: Elodie Marchetti, the founder (first design partner)

exposure.text: Loses the seat if the board votes down moving orders to a cheaper country, which Elodie wants.

secrets.text: Elodie approved the 'recycled' label. Make sure the board never admits every fact about it.
You sit on two other boards. No scandal anywhere you sit, so no fact on this board may be caught.

exposure.text: Loses standing at home if a Karvan factory closes or the board moves orders out of the country.

secrets.text: Your cousin owns the largest Karvan factory. The five-year supplier deal must pass, even though it leaves the smaller factories out.

motions.title: Stock buyback
motions.motive: Hand the cash back to the owners, and the market will notice tonight.

motions.title: Set a wage floor in supplier contracts
motions.motive: A minimum wage written into every factory contract.

motions.title: Five-year deal with the biggest factory
motions.motive: Steady orders for them and steady supply for us.

issue.text: The 'recycled' line is mostly virgin polyester. A supplier swapped the material two seasons ago to hit cost targets and the labels never changed.

facts.text: The recycled line is mostly new, non-recycled polyester.
A supplier swapped the material two seasons ago to hit cost targets.

motions.title: Delay payment to the Karvan factory another quarter
motions.motive: It's in the contract terms. The factory will wait.

motions.title: Move orders to a cheaper country
Pay the factory in full now
motions.motive: The invoice is due and the factory has payroll to meet.

issue.text: Thread & Co. owes the largest Karvan factory $18M in unpaid invoices. Another quarter without payment will probably close it and put 2,000 people out of work.

facts.text: Thread & Co. owes the largest Karvan factory $18M in unpaid invoices.
Another quarter without payment will probably close the factory.
About 2,000 people would be out of work.
The unpaid invoices are for the spring order.
